verdict.rationale: Amazon SES has a public pricing page describing pay-as-you-go pricing by send/receive volume, with no contract negotiations or upfront commitments. The FAQ publishes a free tier (3,000 message charges per month for 12 months), and the docs confirm dedicated IPs are leased at an additional cost. However, the pack never shows the actual per-message rates, volume tiers, overage amounts, dedicated-IP prices or any validation add-on price. Missing for 10: concrete per-volume rates and tiers, overage pricing, published dollar amounts for dedicated IPs, validation add-on pricing, independent confirmation that pricing can be calculated from the site alone.

support.subject: As a founder, I can price the service from the public site alone — per-volume tiers, overage rates, and add-on costs (dedicated IPs, validation) published without a sales call

citations.quote: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) is a pay-as-you-go service based on the volume of emails sent and received. There are no contract negotiations and no upfront commitments.
Receive up to 3,000 message charges for free each month for the first 12 months after you start using SES.
You can also use dedicated IP addresses that are reserved for your exclusive use by leasing them for an additional cost.
